title: When is the Sun closest?
hook: Summer feels like being nearer the Sun. Scrub through the year and check.

knows: that it is hot in summer and cold in winter
that the Earth goes round the Sun once a year
doesNotKnow: where the Earth is on its orbit in each season
how much the Earth-Sun distance varies

misconception: Summer happens because the Earth is closer to the Sun.
objective: The learner can explain that the Earth-Sun distance changes by only about 3% and is smallest in January, so the seasons, which are opposite in the two hemispheres, come from the axial tilt.

claims.text: The Earth is closest to the Sun in early January, at about 147.1 million km.
claims.source: NASA Earth Fact Sheet: perihelion 147.09 x 10^6 km; USNO Earth's Seasons table: perihelion about 2-5 January (date drifts year to year). Lesson model (Kepler ellipse, a = 149.598 Mkm, e = 0.0167, perihelion fixed at 3 Jan) gives 147.10 on day 3: artifacts/scratch/w1-orbit.mjs. Builder could not open the sources (network blocked); figures from the brief and builder recall.

claims.text: The Earth is farthest from the Sun in early July, at about 152.1 million km.
claims.source: NASA Earth Fact Sheet: aphelion 152.10 x 10^6 km; USNO: aphelion about 3-6 July. Lesson model gives 152.10 on day 186 (5 Jul).

claims.text: The distance changes by only about 3% over the year.
claims.source: (152.10 - 147.10) / 149.598 = 3.3%, computed in Demo.tsx from the model's own minimum and maximum.

claims.text: Earth's axis is tilted about 23.4 degrees; on the June solstice the noon Sun is overhead at about 23.4°N.
claims.source: NASA Earth Fact Sheet obliquity 23.44 degrees; IAU / Astronomical Almanac. Subsolar latitude = solar declination, sin(dec) = sin(23.44) sin(ecliptic longitude) (Meeus, Astronomical Algorithms, ch. 25, low-precision).

claims.text: The two hemispheres have opposite seasons: when it is winter in the north it is summer in the south.
claims.source: Any almanac; the stage uses astronomical seasons bounded by equinoxes (about 20 Mar, 22 Sep) and solstices (about 21 Jun, 21 Dec).

claims.text: The orbit drawn on the stage is to scale and looks almost like a circle.
claims.source: Demo.tsx draws r(day) x 100/149.598 px with e = 0.0167; radius ranges 98.3 to 101.7 px. Earth's disc is not to scale (stated on the stage).

claims.text: In June the north pole leans toward the Sun; in December the south pole does.
claims.source: Standard seasons explanation; NASA Space Place 'What causes the seasons?'. Not checked by the builder. | v2 (2026-10-14): claim text rewritten to match the revised stage; previous verification void, needs re-check. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 17): Node with the Demo.tsx orbit model: declination is at least +22.07 deg on every June day and at most -21.82 deg on every December day, so the stage message ('The north/south leans toward the Sun', thresholds +/-5 deg) shows north in June, south in December. Geometry: in June earthLon is about 270 deg, so Earth sits below the Sun and the up-the-page axis arrow points toward it. Agrees with the June solstice subsolar point at 23.4N (c4).

claims.text: The stage names seasons by whole months: March to May is spring, June to August summer, September to November autumn, December to February winter (reversed in the south).
claims.source: Meteorological seasons, the everyday month-based convention (e.g. UK Met Office, NOAA). Implemented in season() in Demo.tsx. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 17): season() in Demo.tsx maps month index 2-4 to spring, 5-7 summer, 8-10 autumn, else winter, swapped for the south. Met Office (metoffice.gov.uk, 'When does Spring start?', 2026 blog; seasons pages) defines meteorological spring as 1 March to 31 May with four three-month seasons.

recall.question: Australia has summer in January. What is the main reason?
options: The Earth is closer to the Sun in January
The southern half of the Earth leans toward the Sun in January
recall.why: Seasons come from the tilt: in January the south leans toward the Sun. The Earth is indeed closest in January, but that is a small effect and the north has winter then.
